name: Granqvist 2005 replication: Thomas right, then burst-firing both sides, sequenced coils
origin: Granqvist, Fredrikson, Unge, Hagenfeldt, Valind, Larhammar & Larsson (Uppsala/Lund), using the DAC010-V sequencer unit and Complex v1.15 software lent by Koren and Persinger (Laurentian University)
summary: A copy, for blinded self-tests, of the Uppsala double-blind test of the God Helmet: 15 min of the Thomas pattern stepped around four right-side coils, then 15 min of burst-firing stepped around both sides, one coil per side at a time, at 5 uT. With 43 people exposed and 46 wearing the helmet without a field, Granqvist et al. 2005 found no effect of the field; absorption, temporal-lobe signs and a New Age orientation predicted sensed presence and mystical experiences.
notes: How this differs from persinger-granqvist-2005-replication: that program drives two static coils per side. The unit lent to Uppsala (a DAC010-V with 4 channels and right and left solenoid sets, SR and SL, created 1998; Persinger, 23 Dec 2004) had a sequencer: the Uppsala team called its 'oscillator' 'the cycling between the solenoids-the four green LED's', in a report Koren quoted and answered on 3 Oct 2003 ('DAC Sequencer Circuit'). Reading the four LEDs as four left-right solenoid pairs, as in the Laurentian helmet, the field here steps around four coils per side; the coil count per side is not published. In the same report Uppsala wrote that the cycling stopped after one to five minutes and that the 'clock' LED ran slightly out of sync with the solenoid LEDs; Koren blamed the computer calibration, a DAC waveform at extreme rates, electrical noise or loose power connections. Whether this was fixed before testing is not published; Granqvist later wrote that 'the diode indicators on the DAC indicated timing in the correct interval' (5 Jan 2005). The Uppsala stepping rate is not published; 0.5 s per position (2 s per turn) with one left and one right solenoid on at a time is the Laurentian helmet as Persinger & Murphy 2016 describe it, and is assumed. Nature reports the fields 'aimed just above and in front of the ears'; T7, FT7, FT9, T9 and their right mirrors (a 2 x 2 square, stepped around in that order) are an inference, as are the stepping order and direction. Phase 1 steps only the right coils (Thomas over the right hemisphere), phase 2 both sides in mirror image (Persinger asked how 'the fields were changed from right hemisphere Thomas to bilateral burstx' and wrote of '15 min of Thomas and 15 min of Burst'); all coils have one polarity. Signals: the Thomas pattern is the exact 849-point patent table at 3 ms with 3 ms between passes (2.55 s per pass, the Laurentian file as Murugan 2013 describes it; Persinger & Murphy 2016: 26 to 8 Hz once every 2 s); that Koren's file was this table is an assumption. Burst-firing point values are unpublished: the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz), 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s; lab theses give 230, 248 or 289 points), once every 3.9 s (Persinger & Murphy 2016: about 1 s every 3 or 4 s; the lab's analgesia work used 4 s): the sequencer had its own oscillator, separate from the pattern (Koren: a DAC waveform at extreme rates 'will cause interference with the sequencer'), and an exact 4 s would land every burst on the same two coil pairs of the 2-s turn, while 3.9 s moves the burst on by 0.1 s each time, so every pair gets it (engine simulation: equal energy on all eight coils). Uppsala ran Complex v1.15, calibrated per its manual, with total cycles set to 9000 'as instructed' (what the software counts as a cycle is not published), and stopped it with ctrl-alt-del after 15 min timed on a digital watch. The field was 3-7 uT; 5 uT is this helmet's maximum. Original design: 89 participants, 43 undergraduates with the field and 46 volunteers wearing the helmet without it (Nature). Double-blind: one experimenter (AH) met the participants and did not know the condition; another (PU) assigned conditions at random and never met them. Participants were told the project concerned 'the influence of complex, weak magnetic fields on experiences and feeling states' (wording quoted by Tinoco & Ortiz 2014 and by Murphy), sat blindfolded (stated in Granqvist's letter, omitted from the paper) in an isolation chamber of about 2 m2, with earplugs according to Persinger's rebuttal (not confirmed by Uppsala), and afterwards rated Persinger's exit list of experiences, translated literally (0 = never, 1 = once or occasionally, 2 = often), and a mystical-experience measure; predictors were the Tellegen Absorption Scale, temporal-lobe signs and a New Age orientation scale. In Nature's account, 2 of the 3 participants who reported strong spiritual experiences, and 11 of the 22 who reported subtle ones, were in the sham group. Persinger & Koren say both groups scored M = 0.3 (SD 0.5) on sensed presence, their usual sham level, and that effective fields give 0.8 or more. They blamed (1) point timing distorted by running the DOS software under Windows on a faster computer than it was written for, (2) 15 min instead of their 20-40 min per pattern, (3) earplugs, a small chamber and no blindfold, and (4) no check of the field before each subject; Granqvist replied that 15 min and 9000 cycles were Persinger's own recommendation, the chamber was about 2 m2, blindfolds were used and the equipment was checked for field output before and after the study. This firmware times every point on a fixed 0.5-ms clock, so objection 1 does not apply to this copy, which for the same reason cannot reproduce any distortion Uppsala's signal may have had; the 15 + 15 min are kept to copy the test. Evidence is single-lab: one double-blind study of this exposure. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (this study; Gendle & McGrath 2012, a different device and signal); Tinoco & Ortiz 2014 reported field-sham differences only in post-session wording. How to run it with the app: on another day, Guides -> Enrollment battery (IPIP Imagination is a free counterpart of the licensed Tellegen scale; the app has no temporal-lobe-signs or New Age scale). For the session a helper who does not know the condition takes AH's role, and the app's Blind option takes PU's: tick Blind in Programs and the helmet's random generator picks real or sham, hidden until you save the rating. Afterwards, first write a free report, then score a fixed list of experiences 0/1/2 (the full exit form is not in the sources used here; Persinger & Murphy 2016 say its 20 items were published by Ruttan, Persinger & Koren 1990; make the sensed-presence item the primary outcome and write down Persinger & Koren's prediction, 0.8 or more with the field against 0.3, before the first session), guess real or sham, and only then save the 0-10 rating; the Log tab keeps condition, rating and Kp. The Experiment tab runs psi trials and is not needed. No medical claim. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on fear or distress.
setting: Blindfolded, seated, in a small (about 2 m2), quiet, dim room, with earplugs (reported only by Persinger's side). The helper says only that the session concerns 'the influence of complex, weak magnetic fields on experiences and feeling states', starts the Blind session, and gives the exit list afterwards without knowing the condition.
schedule: One 30-min session per person in the original (between groups). Self-test: fix the number of Blind sessions in advance (e.g. 10, about half of them sham), at least a day apart, each rated before its reveal; trait questionnaires on a separate day.
